requirements.heading: Where to Send Reports
requirements.text: The Mailbox Provider SHOULD NOT send reports to addresses that have not explicitly requested them.

requirements.heading: What to Put in Reports
requirements.text: The reports SHOULD use "Feedback-Type: abuse" for the report type.

requirements.heading: What to Put in Reports
requirements.text: The following fields are optional in [RFC5965] but SHOULD be used in this context when their corresponding values are available: Original-Mail-From, Arrival-Date, Source-IP, and Original-Rcpt-To.

requirements.heading: What to Put in Reports
requirements.text: User-identifiable data MAY be obscured as described in [RFC6590].

requirements.heading: General Considerations for Feedback Consumers
requirements.text: Operators MUST be able to accept ARF [RFC5965] reports as email messages [RFC5322] over SMTP [RFC5321].

requirements.heading: What to Expect
requirements.text: However, to allow for handling of new types that are not yet supported, an automated report processing system MUST NOT reject (in the SMTP sense) a report based solely on an unknown Feedback-Type.

requirements.heading: What to Expect
requirements.text: Report receivers MUST accept reports that have obscured their user- identifiable data as described in [RFC6590].

requirements.heading: General Considerations
requirements.text: Therefore, Feedback Providers MUST provide a way for report recipients to request that no further reports be sent.

requirements.heading: General Considerations
requirements.text: Therefore, as with any other message, Feedback Providers sending unsolicited reports SHOULD send reports that they expect will pass the Sender Policy Framework (SPF) [RFC4408] and/or DomainKeys Identified Mail (DKIM) [RFC6376] checks.

requirements.heading: When to Generate Reports
requirements.text: Senders of unsolicited reports, especially those sending large volumes of them automatically, SHOULD NOT send reports that cannot be used as a basis for action by the recipient, whether this is due to the report being sent about an incident that is not abuse- related, the report being sent to an email address that won't result in action, or the content or format of the report being hard for the recipient to read or use.

requirements.heading: When to Generate Reports
requirements.text: Feedback Providers SHOULD NOT report all mail sent from a particular sender merely because some of it is determined to be abusive.

requirements.heading: When to Generate Reports
requirements.text: Mechanical reports of mail that "looks like" spam, based solely on the results of inline content analysis tools, SHOULD NOT be sent since, because of their subjective nature, they are unlikely to provide a basis for the recipient to take action.

requirements.heading: When to Generate Reports
requirements.text: Complaints generated by end users about mail that is determined by them to be abusive, or mail delivered to "spam trap" or "honeypot" addresses, are far more likely to be accurate and MAY be sent.

requirements.heading: When to Generate Reports
requirements.text: If a Feedback Provider applies SPF [RFC4408] to arriving messages, a report SHOULD NOT be generated to the RFC5321.MailFrom domain if the SPF evaluation produced a "Fail", "SoftFail", "TempError", or "PermError" report, as no reliable assertion or assumption can be made that use of the domain was authorized.

requirements.heading: Where to Send Reports
requirements.text: Rather than generating feedback reports themselves, MUAs SHOULD create abuse reports and send these reports back to their Mailbox Providers so that they can generate and send ARF messages on behalf of end users (see Section 3.2 of [RFC6449]).

requirements.heading: Where to Send Reports
requirements.text: Feedback Providers SHOULD NOT send reports to recipients that are uninvolved or only peripherally involved.

requirements.heading: Where to Send Reports
requirements.text: For example, they SHOULD NOT send reports to the operator of every Autonomous System in the path between the apparent originating system and the operator

requirements.heading: Where to Send Reports
requirements.text: Unsolicited reports SHOULD NOT be sent to email addresses that are not clearly intended to handle abuse reports.

requirements.heading: Where to Send Reports
requirements.text: Reports SHOULD NOT be sent to such addresses if they can be identified beforehand, except where the abusive party is known to be responsive to such reports.

requirements.heading: What to Put in Reports
requirements.text: Reports SHOULD use "Feedback-Type: abuse" but can use other types as appropriate.

requirements.heading: What to Put in Reports
requirements.text: Reports SHOULD include the following optional fields whenever their corresponding values are available and applicable to the report: Original-Mail-From, Arrival-Date, Source-IP, and Original-Rcpt-To.

requirements.heading: What to Put in Reports
requirements.text: Anyone sending unsolicited reports in ARF can legitimately presume that some recipients will only be able to access the human-readable (first, text/plain) part of it and SHOULD include all information needed also in this part.

requirements.heading: What to Put in Reports
requirements.text: Further, they SHOULD ensure that the report is readable when viewed as plain text, to give low-end ticketing systems as much assistance as possible.

requirements.heading: What to Do with Reports
requirements.text: Per Section 4.4 of [RFC6449], a network service provider MAY use ARF data for automated forwarding of feedback messages to the originating customer.

requirements.heading: What to Do with Reports
requirements.text: Published abuse mailbox addresses SHOULD NOT reject non-ARF messages based solely on the format, as generation of ARF messages can occasionally be unavailable or not applicable.

requirements.heading: What to Do with Reports
requirements.text: Thus, a Feedback Provider sending unsolicited reports SHOULD NOT generate reports for which a reply cannot be received.

requirements.heading: Generating Automatic Authentication Failure Reports
requirements.text: Automatic feedback generators MUST select actual message recipients based on data provided by willing report receivers.

requirements.heading: Generating Automatic Authentication Failure Reports
requirements.text: In particular, recipients MUST NOT be selected using heuristics.

requirements.heading: Generating Automatic Authentication Failure Reports
requirements.text: If the message under evaluation by the Verifier is an ARF [RFC5965] message, a report MUST NOT be automatically generated.

requirements.heading: Generating Automatic Authentication Failure Reports
requirements.text: The message for a new report sent via SMTP MUST be constructed so as to avoid amplification attacks, deliberate or otherwise.

requirements.heading: Generating Automatic Authentication Failure Reports
requirements.text: The envelope sender address of the report MUST be chosen so that these reports will not generate mail loops.

requirements.heading: Generating Automatic Authentication Failure Reports
requirements.text: Similar to Section 2 of [RFC3464], the envelope sender address of the report MUST be chosen to ensure that no feedback reports will be issued in response to the report itself.

requirements.heading: Generating Automatic Authentication Failure Reports
requirements.text: Therefore, when an SMTP transaction is used to send a report, the MAIL FROM command SHOULD use the NULL reverse-path, i.e., "MAIL FROM:<>".

requirements.heading: Generating Automatic Authentication Failure Reports
requirements.text: Reports SHOULD use "Feedback-Type: auth-failure" but MAY use other types as appropriate.

requirements.heading: Generating Automatic Authentication Failure Reports
requirements.text: These reports SHOULD include the following fields, although they are optional in [RFC5965], whenever their corresponding values are available: Original-Mail-From, Arrival-Date, Source-IP, and Original-Rcpt-To.
